I saw this coming in 2007 and tried to warn people, but as expected I was met with laughter. I’m an artist and got a massive exposure to this garbage at one of my gallery shows. I had seen it once before in my first (and last) year at college, I saw what was happening and wanted no part of it so I quit, yet by 2007 it had spilled out of the school system.

The work I had done was immensely popular with the public, yet got me blacklisted and targeted by the local college. Nobody believed what was happening to me and laughed at the notion that liberals would be targeting an artist, so I decided to vanish from the art scene. That’s where this came from.

I’ve watched from the shadows with morbid fascination as this cancer spread into society inch by inch, and the truth is that this what liberals were all along; the things you like about them are just a veneer.

Let me tell you something that exists in every liberal from modern times back to the 1960’s; they have no moral foundation. They are philosophically and spiritually lost, completely, and recoil from objective truth. They are the same people who burned people at the stake and ravaged cities and continents, and are unimaginative hypocrites and degenerates of the lowest order.

Pay attention and you’ll notice their affinity for uniforms, that’s what I noticed that drew me their ire back in 2007.

At the time, there was a zeitgeist that to be an artist meant you were liberal which was ingrained into the public psyche. I, however, was not liberal in any political sense. I had many liberal tendencies and views, but I understood that they weren’t feasible for society to adopt as a whole. The work I displayed in that showing was centered around flipping liberal ideas on their head, but doing so through a means (art) that was considered liberal. The centerpiece was a 7’x5’ painting which mocked what is known as a “cotillion”; a high-society event where wealthy spawn are introduced into the social sphere of adulthood (like a gentile version of a barmitzvah). It featured a knight riding a massive ogre into a coliseum of topless harlots. Another was of an embrace between a centurion and a woman (romanticism), and another was of a demon hiding in a circuit board.

I found out years later from my old high school art teacher that my exhibition accounted for 90% of the student analysis papers during time from the nearby college (out of 12 artists total, 3 of which were international). This is probably what irked them the most, seeing as I was the only artist represented who did not have a college education.
